chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Dāwūd al-Ṣarmī, who said: Bashīr ibn Bashshār narrated to me, saying:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in al-fanak, al-firāʾ, al-sinjāb, al-sammūr, and al-ḥawāṣil that are hunted in the lands of shirk or the lands of Islam: may I perform salat (prayer) in it without taqiyyah?
He said, so he said: “Perform salat (prayer) in al-sinjāb and the Khwārazmian al-ḥawāṣil, and do not perform salat (prayer) in fox furs nor in al-sammūr.”

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: fox furs, ruled impermissible here for prayer
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable fur, ruled impermissible here for prayer
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel fur, ruled permissible here for prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْحَوَاصِلِ: a type of pelt or fur mentioned as permissible in a specific form
key_terms.الْفَنَكِ: a type of fur-bearing animal whose pelt is asked about for use in prayer
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation/precautionary concealment, here indicating the ruling when not acting under taqiyyah

ai.seo_question: Which animal furs are permissible or impermissible to wear during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on which animal furs or pelts may be worn in salat (prayer). It permits salat (prayer) in squirrel fur and Khwārazmian pelts, while prohibiting it in fox and sable fur, indicating distinctions in permissible prayer garments within fiqh.
